text: When Tom asked who he was, the stranger said that he went by many names, and Tom realized that he was talking to Old Scratch, the devil himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Meeting such a figure would have frightened most men, but Tom had lived so long with a fierce wife that he did not fear even the devil. <break time="0.8s" /> Old Scratch offered him Kidds treasure on certain conditions, which must have been hard, since Tom asked for time to think them over. <break time="0.8s" /> As proof, the devil pressed a finger on Toms forehead, and when Tom got home, he found a black fingerprint burned into his skin. <break time="0.8s" /> Tom told his wife the whole secret, and she, greedy for the hidden gold, urged him to accept the bargain at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Out of pure stubbornness Tom refused, so she decided to make the deal herself and keep all the gold for herself. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening she set off for the swamp with the silver teapot and spoons tied up in her apron, and she never came back. <break time="0.8s" /> Searching for her at last, Tom found her apron hanging in a tree, and the ground below was trampled as if by a fierce struggle. <break time="0.8s" /> Seeing clumps of black hair there, Tom guessed that she had fought the devil hard, and the loss of his wife made up for the loss of his silver.
